Medicine
Medicine
Prepare to become a medical practitioner or researcher. Gain the skills to further scientific research or work within the current healthcare environment.
At St Andrews, a highly supportive educational environment provides you with the necessary training to start your professional career.
We offer ScotGEM, ScotCOM, undergraduate degrees in medicine, and postgraduate degrees in health data science and health professions education, as well as stand-alone modules in health professions education.

Supported pathway
The Gateway to Medicine provides supported entry into degree-level study for applicants who do not meet the minimum entry grades but meet contextual criteria.
International Foundation programmes
International Foundation programmes enable international students from a wide range of countries to develop the necessary skills to meet the demands of an undergraduate degree programme across subjects and disciplines at the University of St Andrews.

Postgraduate research
The School of Medicine offers PhD and MSc (Res) research degree programmes in medicine. Research interests within the School are typically divided into four areas:
cellular medicine
education
infection and global health
population and behavioural science.
See current postgraduate research opportunities for information on available supervision topics and how to apply.
Stand-alone modules
Open all
Explore modules
We offer a range of stand-alone online modules in health professions education, each accredited at SCQF Level 11. These part-time, 15-credit modules run from September to December and are delivered entirely online. They include approximately two hours of synchronous online teaching every fortnight, supplemented by self-study.
These modules allow you to explore specialist topics within health professions education and can also serve as an introduction or return to academic study at this postgraduate level.

I like that we get exposure to a hospital setting early on in the course as well as learning the different clinical skills that are involved. The University staff are amazing people - they are kind, helpful, friendly, and they care about you.”
Xu Xuan
- Penang, Malaysia
School of Medicine
The School of Medicine’s curriculum is designed to meet the General Medical Council’s (GMC) aspirations for future teaching. The School is based in the Medical and Biological Sciences Building which is superbly equipped with a dissecting room, clinical skills suite, anatomy resource centre and more.
Visit St Andrews
If you’re interested in studying at St Andrews, join us at a visiting day or talk and tour to explore the town, find out about our courses and meet current students. You can also join us for one of our upcoming online events.
